events.title: Bush by one point
events.text: George W. Bush carried New Hampshire by 1.3 points, the last Republican presidential win there.

events.title: A senator's primary loss
events.text: John E. Sununu, a congressman since 1997, beat Senator Bob Smith in the Republican primary.

events.title: Sununu beats Shaheen
events.text: Sununu beat Governor Jeanne Shaheen for the U.S. Senate, 51.1 to 46.7 percent.

events.title: Kerry carries it
events.text: John Kerry carried New Hampshire by 1.4 points; Democrats have won it for president ever since.

events.title: Berlin mill closes
events.text: The pulp mill in Berlin, long the North Country's largest employer, closed.

events.title: The rematch
events.text: Shaheen unseated Sununu, 51.6 to 45.3 percent, becoming the first woman elected both governor and senator.

events.title: Obama by ten
events.text: Barack Obama carried the state by 9.6 points.

events.title: Pappas on the Council
events.text: Chris Pappas, of Manchester, was elected to the five-member Executive Council.

events.title: All-female delegation
events.text: New Hampshire became the first state with an all-female congressional delegation.

events.title: Trump wins the primary
events.text: Donald Trump won the Republican presidential primary with 35 percent.

events.title: 1,017 votes
events.text: Maggie Hassan unseated Senator Kelly Ayotte by 1,017 votes.

events.title: Governor Sununu
events.text: Chris Sununu, John E. Sununu's brother, was elected governor; he won four terms.

events.title: 2,736 votes
events.text: Hillary Clinton carried New Hampshire by 0.4 points.

events.title: Pappas to Congress
events.text: Pappas won the 1st District, the first openly gay man elected to Congress from New Hampshire.

events.title: Shaheen re-elected
events.text: Shaheen won a third term by almost sixteen points; Joe Biden carried the state by 7.4.

events.title: Split tickets
events.text: Hassan was re-elected by 9 points while Governor Sununu won by 15.5.

events.title: “We're going to lose”
events.text: Backing Nikki Haley, John E. Sununu wrote in the Union Leader that with Donald Trump as nominee “we're going to lose bad.”

events.title: Harris and Ayotte
events.text: Kamala Harris carried New Hampshire by 2.8 points; Kelly Ayotte, a Republican, won the governorship by 9.3.

events.title: No income-type tax
events.text: The tax on interest and dividends was repealed; the state taxes neither wages nor general sales.

events.title: Shaheen retires
events.text: On 12 March Shaheen said she would not seek re-election: “It's just time.”

events.title: Pappas runs
events.text: On 3 April Pappas launched his Senate campaign in Manchester.

events.title: Chris Sununu declines
events.text: In April former Governor Chris Sununu said he would not run for the Senate.

events.title: Brown runs
events.text: In June Scott Brown, a former Massachusetts senator and Trump's ambassador to New Zealand, entered the Republican primary.

events.title: Sununu returns
events.text: On 22 October John E. Sununu entered the race for the seat he lost in 2008.

events.title: Trump endorses Sununu
events.text: On 1 February President Trump endorsed Sununu.

events.title: Hampton debate
events.text: Sununu and Brown met in an NHPR primary debate in Hampton.

events.title: August polls
events.text: A UNH poll had Sununu ahead by two; a Saint Anselm poll had Pappas ahead by seven.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 8 September Sununu beat Brown, 68 to 27 percent; Pappas beat Karishma Manzur, 65 to 33.

events.title: Pappas pulls ahead
events.text: UNH's September poll had Pappas ahead, 50 to 42 percent.

events.title: Two ad campaigns
events.text: Party-aligned groups have reserved tens of millions in advertising; outside spending reached about $50 million.

events.title: A tax fact-check
events.text: PolitiFact rated false Sununu's claim that Pappas voted to raise taxes 68 times.

events.title: A Social Security check
events.text: PolitiFact rated mostly true Pappas's claim that Sununu led efforts to privatize Social Security.

events.title: An Amazon fact-check
events.text: PolitiFact rated mostly false a Republican super PAC's claim that Pappas lied about dating an Amazon lobbyist.

events.title: First debate
events.text: On 13 October the nominees debated in North Conway; WMUR and NHPR debates follow on 28 and 29 October.

events.title: The ratings
events.text: In October Cook rated the race Lean Democratic, Sabato Likely Democratic and Inside Elections Tilt Democratic.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November voters choose between Pappas, Sununu and LaPlante; New Hampshire has no early voting.

eras: Split tickets and an open seat
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; certified results). It is a simplification: New Hampshire elects its senator in its own race, and many voters split their tickets (in 2024 Kamala Harris won the state by 2.8 points while a Republican won the governorship by 9.3), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on New Hampshire, so outer states are cut at the edge.
